 For Petitioner : Mr.R.Vivekanandan  for Mr.B.Ravi  For Respondents : M/s.M.Jayanthy  Additional Government Pleader  ORDER

This Writ Petition has been filed seeking for issuance of a mandamus, to direct the respondents 2 and 3 to make the reference, under Section 20(1) of Tamil Nadu Highways Act to the appropriate Court as per the representation sent by the petitioner dated 22.03.2019 with reference to the issue of enhancement of compensation in respect of the petitioner lands in New S.No.190/35 measuring 310 sq.meter, Oragadam Village, Sriperumpudur Taluk, Kancheepuram District.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 2.

The case of the petitioner is that originally the property is situated at S.No.190/28, New S.No.190/36 and 190/35 measuring to an extent of 4050 sq.mts which was purchased by the petitioner's grandfather.
After his lifetime, it devolved upon the petitioner's father.
After the demise of his father, the property devolved on the legal heirs of T.Jayaraman.

The said property was divided by metes and bounds through a Registered Partition Deed dated 04.12.2003 and thus being the legal heirs of T.Jayaraman, the petitioner has became the owner of 25 cents in New S.No.190/35 and his brother became the owner of 75 cents in New S.No.190/36 and S.No.190/35 out of one acre in Oragadam Village.

From and out of the 25 cents of land allotted to the petitioner under the partition deed, the Highways Department vide Notification dated 09.08.2017 sought to acquire 310 sq.mts in S.No.190/35 under Section 15(2) of the Tamil Nadu Highways Act.
Subsequent to the Notification under Section 15(2) of the Act, the petitioner did not received any communication from the respondents herein in respect of the said acquisition under Act 34 of 2002.

sentences.text: 4. On 28.02.2019/01.03.2019, the fourth respondent passed an Award.
In view of the request of the respondents, the petitioner had agreed to received the compensation under protest with a request for reference of the matter under Section 20 of the Act, on 22.03.2019.
The respondents paid the compensation to the petitioner through Cheque dated 28.08.2019 and the same was handed over to the petitioner on 13.09.2019.
He has also received a notice on 20.09.2019 seeking to handover the area of land under acquisition.

5. Since the compensation amount paid to the petitioner is not in accordance with the present prevailing market value, and that the respondents are ignoring to make a reference, as requested by the petitioner under Section 20 of the Act, he caused a legal notice seeking either to accept the return of compensation paid or in the alternative to make a reference as per the petitioner's r e p r e s e n t a t i o n d a t e d 2 2 . 0 3 . 2 0 1 9 , a s p r e s c r i b e d u n d e r S e c t i o n 2 0 o f https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis the Act.
After receipt of the notice, the fourth respondent replied stating that the compensation amount paid cannot be received back.
Hence, the writ petition.
6. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Additional Government Pleader for the respondents.

7. A status report was filed by the fourth respondent dated 30.01.2020, wherein, it is mentioned that necessary proposal has been submitted in his office Lr.No.27/2017 dated 24.01.2020 to the first respondent for referring the matter to the concerned Sub Court.
But, till now, the first respondent has not passed any order for referring the matter before the appropriate Court.

8. Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case, the second and third respondents are directed to make a reference under Section 20(1) of the Act to the appropriate Court, as per the representation of the petitioner dated 22.03.2019 with reference to the issue of enhancement of compensation in respect of the petitioner's land in S.No.190/35 measuring an extent of 310 sq.meter at Oragadam Village, Sriperumbudur Taluk, Kancheepuram District, within a period of three months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order. https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 9.
This writ petition is disposed of with the above observations.
No costs.
